title: KV signal factorization and bank-aware guardrail prototype
body:
Purpose:
Quick experimental note on factoring KV cache signals into orthogonal components and using bank-local bandwidth as a guardrail to avoid eviction thrash under multi-tenant surge. Goal is to reduce tail latency and noisy NVMe paging without over-constraining throughput.

Background / motivation:
- We see repeated incidents where p99 spikes correlate with a subset of keys being heavily reaccessed but not pinned, causing eviction churn and NVMe writeback spikes.
- Prior approaches (global priority score, simple pin thresholds) reduce tails but either waste pin budget or create starvation under bank contention.
- Hypothesis: decomposing signals into short-term reuse intent (temporal locality) + long-term hotness (steady popularity) and combining that with per-memory-bank BW slack yields a better, adaptive admission/eviction policy.

Signals we instrumented (telemetry):
- access_count_ewma (per-key, alpha=0.2) -> short-term reuse proxy
- lifetime_hits (total since load) -> long-term hotness
- last_access_delta histogram -> capture burstiness
- per-bank bandwidth_util (GB/s) and qdepth
- nvme_writeback_rate (ops/s)
- eviction_cause tag (pressure|manual|pin)
- request_tail_latency at the request tag level

Signal factorization idea:
1) Short-term reuse score S = normalized access_count_ewma * f1(last_access_delta)
2) Long-term hotness H = log(1 + lifetime_hits) normalized by tenant
3) Bank pressure P_b = 1 - min(1, bandwidth_util_b / safe_bw_b)
4) Effective priority = S * (1 + beta * H) * (1 - gamma * P_b)
Where beta,gamma are tunable. The (1 - gamma*P_b) term is the bank-aware guardrail: when a bank is saturated, we lower effective priority to avoid additional prefetch/paging that would worsen bandwidth.

Prototype implementation notes:
- Implemented as a small extension to the existing admission path. Kept computation per-chunk (1000 keys) to amortize cost.
- Maintains per-bank exponential moving average of bandwidth per second, reset at 30s windows on config change.
- Prefetches are gated by a per-bank token bucket that consumes tokens proportional to expected bytes.
- When a key is admitted and flagged high-priority, we try to pin it iff global_pin_budget > threshold and local_bank_tokens available.

Synthetic workload (kv-randwalk-v2) config used for experiments:
- 80% reads, 20% writes
- 200k keyspace, working set hot fraction configurable (0.5% to 5%)
- Bursty clients: Poisson arrivals with 50ms bursts every 10s
- Multi-tenant mix: 3 tenants where tenant0 has hotset=0.5%, tenant1 dynamic spikes, tenant2 steady background

Key results (summary):
- Baseline (current LRU-like + global priority): p99 request latency during tenant spikes = 420ms, NVMe writebacks = 3600 ops/min, paging miss rate = 12.4%
- Prototype: p99 = 345ms (-17.9%), NVMe writebacks = 2750 ops/min (-23.6%), paging miss rate = 9.1% (-26.6%)
- Impact on p50: slight increase from 18ms to 19ms due to extra checks (+5.5%)
- CPU overhead: +3.8% on the admission thread, memory overhead negligible (extra counters ~2MB per host)

Observed failure modes / caveats:
- If beta too high (over-emphasis on long-term hotness) we see pin over-commit and starvation of new bursts.
- Guardrail reacts to sustained bank pressure; very short spikes (<1s) are not prevented and can still cause transient paging blips.
- Multi-tenant misalignment where tenants map many hot keys into same bank (bank skew) still causes outage-like degradation; bank-aware guardrail helps but does not fully mitigate worst-case colocation.

Microbench traces that were interesting:
- Trace A (tenant spike): eviction_cause switched from 'pressure' to 'pin' mid-window — indicates pin budget hit.
- Trace B (bank saturation): per-bank queue depth rose before writebacks increased, confirming bandwidth queueing precedes NVMe overhead.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tune alpha/beta/gamma via automated grid search with reinforcement objective (minimize p99 + cost penalty).
- Add bank-aware placement during shuffle/reshard to reduce hot key colocation (solution might live in placement service).
- Longer run: integrate with rollout toggles and canary fraction (console/rollouts product) so we can A/B test with real traffic.
- Add synthetic scenario where prefetch is disabled to isolate effect of prefetch gating.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Share telemetry dashboard sample (Evan) -> linear ENG-6132
- [ ] Open PR to add per-bank token bucket and config knobs (Jonah) -> github PR linked above
- [ ] Run 24h multi-tenant soak with realistic tenant map (Mariana)
- [ ] Add automated regression in perf-suite measuring NVMe writebacks and p99 under two burst shapes

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Could combine with small RL agent that nudges gamma per bank on 1-minute intervals; keep as fallback, not primary control.
- Consider exposing a "bank pressure" metric in Console so customers can see why pinned keys may be demoted under heavy IO.
- Slack thread: #kv-telemetry had some chatter about making safe_bw_b tenant-configurable — might be useful for large enterprise customers with reserved NVMe QoS.

References and links (work items):
- linear ENG-6132 (telemetry matrix)
- perf harness branch: github.com/redwood-inference/perf/kv-randwalk-v2
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427

Summary: prototype looks promising — solid reduction in p99 and NVMe writebacks with small cost. Next: broader soak, auto-tune parameter sweep, and explore placement changes to reduce bank skew.

-- Asha
